Law Passed: California SB 54 (Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act, enacted June 2022) — final implementing regulations effective May 1, 2026; enforcement active; now facing multiple legal challenges including a preliminary injunction motion filed August 20, 2026 seeking to block the entire law.
Status Detail: Final SB 54 regulations were approved by the California Office of Administrative Law on May 1, 2026 and became immediately effective, triggering producer registration and reporting obligations (deadline June 1, 2026). The law now faces two parallel legal challenges: a state court suit filed June 2, 2026 by NRDC and allied environmental groups alleging the regulations are insufficiently protective, and a federal constitutional challenge filed June 22, 2026 by a 17-state AG coalition and NAW. On August 20, 2026, the federal plaintiffs escalated by filing a motion for preliminary injunction in the Eastern District of California seeking to suspend enforcement of the entire Act; a hearing is scheduled for January 15, 2027. No injunction has been granted and compliance obligations remain in effect.

Law Passed: Georgia HB 1237 (Pollution Prevention and Producer Responsibility Act of 2026), which would have established a comprehensive EPR framework for packaging, paper products, and beverage containers, was introduced February 6, 2026 and died in committee during the 2026 legislative session. Status Detail: HB 1237 covered all covered packaging materials (including bags, film, paper, and other packaging types) and would have created Producer Responsibility Organizations, an advisory board, recycling/composting standards, and enforcement requirements. Separately, SR 610 — a Senate Study Committee on Improving and Increasing Recycling — passed the Georgia Senate 48-0 on March 31, 2026, and will convene during the interim; this is widely noted as the typical precursor step taken by states that have later enacted EPR laws.

Law Passed: Hawaii HB 750 signed into law May 27, 2025 — requires the state Department of Health to conduct a statewide needs assessment for packaging materials and paper products EPR program; no comprehensive EPR program enacted. A separate full EPR bill (HB 1264, 2025 session) covering primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging including bags did not advance. In March 2026, four non-binding resolutions were introduced directing the DoH to study recyclable, biodegradable, and compostable labeling; no new EPR bills enacted in 2026.
Status Detail: HB 750 (signed May 27, 2025) is the operative Hawaii law: it directs the Department of Health to conduct a statewide needs assessment for a potential packaging EPR program covering packaging materials and paper products, funded at $1.5 million annually for FY 2026 and 2027, with the final report due to the legislature by December 31, 2027. The DoH began assessment work in July 2025 and is establishing an Advisory Council. No comprehensive EPR program with producer fees or registration obligations has been enacted; further EPR legislation is listed as pending by O'Melveny (April 2026) but no new bill has passed.

Law Passed: Maine's packaging EPR law (originally LD 1541, enacted 2021) was amended by LD 1423, signed June 20, 2025. Implementation is now in jeopardy: the RFP for a Stewardship Organization closed August 18, 2026 with zero proposals submitted, and DEP is determining next steps.
Status Detail: Maine DEP issued its long-delayed Stewardship Organization RFP on June 15, 2026, with proposals due August 18, 2026; no electronic submissions were received by the deadline, leaving the program without an administrator. Law Passed: Maryland SB 901 (Packaging and Paper Products Producer Responsibility Plan) was signed into law on May 13, 2025. MDE finalized the first set of implementing regulations, effective May 25, 2026. Producer registration and simplified supply reporting deadlines passed on May 31 / July 1, 2026.
Status Detail: Maryland SB 901 is fully enacted and in active implementation. The Maryland Department of the Environment adopted initial EPR regulations on May 5, 2026, published in the Maryland Register on May 15, 2026, and effective May 25, 2026. A sales ban on non-compliant covered materials takes effect October 29, 2028 (or later date set by MDE), and a full five-year Producer Responsibility Plan is due from PROs by July 1, 2028.

Law Passed: North Carolina HB 882 (Break Free From Plastic & Forever Chemicals Act), filed April 2025, is pending in the House Rules Committee with no passage.
Status Detail: HB 882, introduced April 9, 2025, would establish a comprehensive packaging EPR framework requiring producers to register with NCDEQ and join a Producer Responsibility Organization, mandate phased reductions in non-reusable packaging (10% after two years, up to 40% after eight years), and ban toxic substances including PFAS, phthalates, lead, and mercury from packaging materials — covering all packaging types including plastic film, bags, and other packaging formats. The bill has been referred to and remains stalled in the House Rules, Calendar, and Operations Committee as of the most recent reporting (July 2026). An earlier version of the bill (H 279, 2023 session) died in the same committee.

Law Passed: Oklahoma has no enacted EPR packaging law. HB 4068, an environmental marketing claims / packaging labeling bill introduced in February 2026, died in committee when the Oklahoma legislature adjourned sine die in May 2026 without a floor vote.
Status Detail: Oklahoma HB 4068 (introduced February 2026) would have prohibited unsubstantiated environmental claims — including recyclable, compostable, biodegradable, and sustainability claims — on products and packaging sold in the state. Law Passed: Rhode Island H 6207 (needs assessment law) signed June 30, 2025; full EPR bills H.B. 7910, S.B. 2656, and S.B. 7911 introduced in February 2026 and remain pending in committee.
Status Detail: H 6207, signed by Governor McKee on June 30, 2025, mandates a third-party statewide recycling and waste-management gap analysis with a needs assessment report due December 1, 2026, to inform potential future EPR legislation. In the 2026 session, three new full EPR bills (H.B. 7910, S.B. 2656, and S.B. 7911) were introduced on February 27, 2026; H.B. 7910 received a committee hearing on May 27, 2026, while S.B. 2656 remained under committee review — both held amid concerns over infrastructure readiness and distributor costs. Rhode Island is not expected to pass a full EPR law in 2026, with the active needs assessment framing any comprehensive legislation as a 2027–2028 prospect.

Law Passed: Vermont S.139 (2025-2026 session), 'An act relating to the management of materials from packaging,' was introduced April 2, 2025, and stalled in the Senate Committee on Natural Resources and Energy without advancing. A companion House bill, H.139 (same session), similarly did not advance out of committee. No comprehensive EPR packaging law has been enacted in Vermont. Separately, H.915 (Act 158), an EPR program for beverage containers (not general shipping/packaging materials such as poly bags, film, paper, or mesh), was signed by the Governor on June 17, 2026.
Status Detail: Vermont's broad packaging EPR bill S.139, which would have required a needs assessment covering packaging materials including opportunities to improve reuse, recyclability, and reduce toxicity and quantity, died in the Senate Committee on Natural Resources and Energy during the 2025-2026 session. No comprehensive EPR packaging law covering shipping and distribution packaging (poly bags, film, paper, mesh) has been enacted. The Proskauer July 2026 update confirms Vermont is in the 'could see a bill go all the way in 2027 or 2028' category but has not passed packaging EPR.

Law Passed: Virginia has no enacted EPR packaging law. At least one EPR packaging bill introduced in the 2026 General Assembly session carried over and remains active into 2027, making Virginia one of only two states (alongside New Jersey) with a bill in carryover status.
Status Detail: The 2026 Virginia General Assembly adjourned sine die on March 14, 2026 without passing an EPR packaging law. Virginia is one of only two states where an EPR packaging bill carried over from the 2026 session into 2027 rather than dying at adjournment; all other states must fully reintroduce bills in 2027. Any carried-over bill not acted upon by the November 2026 deadline will die before the 2027 session begins.

Law Passed: Washington E2SSB 5284 (Recycling Reform Act), signed into law May 17, 2025, establishing a statewide EPR program for residential packaging and paper products (Chapter 70A.208 RCW). Implementation is actively underway: Circular Action Alliance (CAA) was designated as the PRO in March 2026, the producer registration deadline (July 1, 2026) has passed, and Ecology opened a public comment period (Aug. 5–19, 2026) on preliminary statewide collection lists. Covered materials include glass, plastic (including film/flexible packaging), paper, and metal packaging used to protect, contain, transport, or facilitate delivery of consumer products.
Status Detail: The law is in Phase 1 implementation. CAA is the designated PRO; producers were required to join by July 1, 2026. Ecology is conducting rulemaking, has published preliminary statewide collection lists for public comment (Aug. 5–19, 2026), and must finalize those lists by October 1, 2026. Full program operation, including cost reimbursement to recycling service providers, begins January 1, 2030.
